title: Long-Running Work and the Tasks Extension

questions.question: Why can a server not just hold the connection open until a twenty-minute pipeline finishes?
options: Transport timeouts, no input channel during execution, and no crash recovery at all
Because MCP requires every tool call to use the tasks extension for any tool
Because the client always closes the connection after exactly one request completes
Because JSON-RPC forbids any request from taking longer than one second to answer
questions.explanation: Blocking runs into transport timeouts that are not the server's to set, no channel to ask for input mid-call, and no way to recover after a crash or dropped connection.

questions.question: Where does a client declare support for io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks on a given request?
options: In the tasks field of the tools/list response the server returned earlier
In that request's own params._meta, under clientCapabilities.extensions field
In a session header the server issues after the first successful tool call
In a one-time initialize handshake that both sides remember for the connection
questions.explanation: Extension support is declared per request in clientCapabilities.extensions inside params._meta, because there is no session or handshake that would let the server remember an earlier declaration.

questions.question: A tasks/get response shows resultType complete and, nested inside it, status working. What does that combination mean?
options: Both the poll request and the underlying job have now fully finished
The client must resend tools/call to keep the underlying job moving forward
The poll request itself succeeded, but the underlying job is still running
The server rejected the poll because the task is not ready to be read
questions.explanation: tasks/get always completes, so its own resultType is complete; the job's real state travels in the separate, nested status field, which here still says working.

questions.question: A task moves to input_required and tasks/get returns an inputRequests map. How does the client respond?
options: It waits, since input_required tasks resume automatically without any reply at all
It retries the original tools/call with a new id and the same inputRequests key
It sends a fresh elicitation/create request directly to the server on its own
It sends tasks/update with inputResponses keyed to the still outstanding entries
questions.explanation: Task input is answered through tasks/update with inputResponses keyed to the outstanding entries; the client never resends the original tools/call for this.

questions.question: A tools/call finishes with isError true inside its content. What status does its task reach?
options: completed, because the tool call still produced its own normally defined result
cancelled, because an error inside a result counts as an implicit cancellation
input_required, because the model must approve the error before it counts at all
failed, because any error anywhere in the result is treated as a JSON-RPC failure
questions.explanation: A tool result with isError true is still a successful protocol exchange, so the task reaches completed; failed is reserved for a JSON-RPC error during execution, not a tool-level failure.

questions.question: Which piece of work is the best fit for the tasks extension rather than a plain call or an MRTR round trip?
options: Reading one resource whose contents never change between separate requests
A deploy pipeline that may pause for approval and could outlive a timeout
Listing the tools a server currently exposes to a newly connecting client
Asking the user to confirm a single value before finishing the current request
questions.explanation: A task earns its added complexity when work might outlive a timeout, pause for input mid-execution, or need to survive a restart or cancellation, unlike the other options here.
